AMERICAS TECHNOLOGY: INTERNET
US Digital Ad Q3’25 Preview: Analyzing the Industry Debates & Estimates
We preview Q3 2025 earnings season for the digital advertising sub-sector of our coverage universe. We also make two stock recommendation changes: we downgrade MAX from Buy to Neutral with a 12-month price target of \$12.00 (from \$14.50 prior) and downgrade IBTA from Neutral to Sell with a 12-month price target of \$26 (from \$30 prior). Finally, in a companion note (link), we assume coverage of Unity (U) from Kash Rangan with a Neutral rating (unchanged) and 12-month price target of \$38 (from \$32.50 prior).
Across our coverage universe we make a series of operating estimate changes to highlight a mix of: a) sustained momentum around performance-oriented budgets (direct response channels) throughout Q3, with heightened performance in July/August; b) continued industry headwinds from a weaker brand advertising environment (especially from large advertisers) with easing revenue headwinds emerging in September that might act an improved tailwind (or at least easier comps) in Q4 2025; & c) experimental budgets that remain more volatile with smaller platforms still seeing more stalled or downside volatility to budgets in the September timeframe. In addition, visibility levels in forward spend remain low – most advertising industry checks don’t yet have a good read on how the ad budget cycle for 2026 might be framed (even though many conversations on such budget allocations will kick off in the November/December timeframe). In addition, the value of programmatic platforms (Meta’s Advantage+, Alphabet’s Performance Max, AppLovin’s Axon 2.0, Pinterest’s Performance+, etc.) continue to scale and take share of industry budgets as elements of automation and quantitative framing remains attractive to many advertiser cohorts.
In terms of performance by industry vertical, we highlight a few takeaways from our advertising industry conversations:
n Retail & eCommerce advertisers continue to deploy marketing dollars against stable end demand trends, especially in certain verticals that are less discretionary and skew to certain household income levels where spending trends are currently less volatile. Q3 industry checks show some return of global eCommerce advertisers to performance channels in the US with sustained marketing intensity across non-US markets (a reversal of a headwind to industry trends in Q2).

Online Travel is normalizing around more mid to high single digital industry growth in 2H 2025 and marketing budgets are adjusting accordingly. The industry sees more robust activity levels across high income households and travel trends (luxury) are more supportive of growth investments than other household income levels (with shorter duration stays and higher cancellation rates).
Autos spend was stable QoQ and more in line with usual seasonality in Q3 based on industry volume levels and incentives across both the new/used markets.
n CPG (household products & food/beverage) showed a mixture of more stable marketing trends, easier comps, and the continued rise of emerging brands (especially challenger DTC brands) as a percentage of spend mix. The vertical will mark watching on easier comps in 2H 2025 as overall spend levels remain muted but YoY growth rates might be flattered as we lap 12–24-month muted spending levels.
Key industry themes that have moved back to the forefront of industry conversations (some of which were on display at the recent Adweek events in NYC in early October) include:
n Increasing adoption/utilization of AI/machine learning-driven programmatic systems and ad products (GOOGL’s Performance Max; META’s Advantage+; etc.), - a theme that we continue to highlight as underappreciated and under-modeled across Street estimates.
Budget shifts toward direct response/performance channels (over brand). The only contrary point to raise here is that some distinct brands have reinvested search spend into brand name investments across multiple channels as some headwinds to referral traffic from certain channels (e.g. search) have emerged.
n Growth from emerging channels including retail media networks, Connected TV (CTV)/Ad-Supported Video On Demand (AVOD) and other video advertising formats and creator/influence marketing.
With respect to how the AI theme translates into the search landscape specifically (a key investor debate currently), we believe a few key variables remain important to monitor in the quarters ahead:
The rate of platform/product adoption by consumers across OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Meta AI, Perplexity, Anthropic’s Claude, Grok AI, etc.
n With respect to product adoption, OpenAI’s recent Developer Day and Shopping launch (with Shopify and Etsy as initial partners) have caused outsized stock performance volatility as it has again raised open ended investor questions about how agentic consumer behavior and any potential shifts toward agentic commerce (broadly defined) might impact current Internet funnel behavior (from brand to direct response).
n Whether the competitive dynamics around such products evolve to alter commercial queries and whether the landscape moves toward a “winner takes most” outcome.
How existing search product evolution (e.g., AI Overviews and AI Mode for Google) impacts the current base of advertising budget trends with respect to search.

n We have not yet seen any commercial query or query monetization disruption to Google Search from AI to date, even as user adoption/query volumes on both Google’s own AI products (AI Overviews, AI Mode & Gemini) and competitors has increased significantly. That said, the specter of changed consumer behaviors on intent-based commercial queries remains a variable that investors view as potentially disruptive to industry norms.
Company Ratings & Estimates Changes - We make several ratings changes with this preview as a result of changes to our forward operating estimates and PTs across the board. Overall, we’d characterize these estimates changes as follows:
We expect companies will report Q3 advertising trends toward the upper band/modestly above guided ranges (if provided) from the last earnings season, with healthy direct-response trends in July/August and easing brand ad headwinds in September driving revenue growth momentum for the industry.
n We expect ad trends to remain solid into the seasonally-strong Q4 holiday season with these same dynamics continuing (direct response-led growth, with brand ad trends more volatile/dependent on macro dynamics and YoY comps). That said, visibility remains low and we therefore see potential for ad trends to be volatile through Q4 and into 2026 depending on many factors (industry vertical exposure, ad objective exposure, AI vs. non-AI automation, performance by channel, macroeconomic and consumer spending environments, etc.).
With respect to the mobile app advertising environment, in this note and in our companion U report (link), we outline the current growth outlook for AppLovin’s AXON 2.0 and Unity’s Vector and provide estimates around the current expected revenue contribution for both AI platforms in the coming years. We expect APP to continue to take share of mobile in-game advertising dollars (particularly into the launch of their self-serve platform for eCommerce advertisers), but also expect U to grow share (off a lower base) as Vector scales in the coming quarters.
n On expenses, while advertising operating trends are on a firmer footing than when we published our last quarterly preview, we still expect a central theme in the upcoming earnings season to be how companies balance growth investments (especially around AI and ad tech implementation) against revenue trends (as it relates to visibility into forward EPS growth).
Stock Recommendations - We continue to be constructive across the digital advertising sub-sector on a longer-term basis and highlight Buy-rated large cap stocks, META and GOOGL. For both stocks, we expect investors to remain focused on the elevated level of AI-related capex that the large-cap tech platforms are currently undergoing - how each company frames a mixture of operating efficiencies against levels/scope of investments is likely to be a key determinant of short-term stock performance as the macroeconomic outlook remains less visible in terms of framing forward growth trajectories. After META’s mgmt team gave visibility into 2026 opex and capex plans on the last earnings call, we have received increased questions on the potential for an upward trajectory to AI investment cycle (including for GOOGL). In addition, with private companies (such as OpenAI and Anthropic) also sustaining elevated capex levels, we have gotten increased questions about the sustainability and return profile of such spend in the coming years

n Meta Platforms (META, Buy, \$870 PT) – For META, we have seen a sustained upward operating trend line in our intra quarter industry work with momentum building in terms of both engagement and monetization trends – in our view, both dynamics put an upward pressure on revenue trends relative to Street estimates. In the last few weeks, two investor debates have emerged that have been putting pressure on short-term share performance: 1) Will industry-wide capex trends (especially long-term deals for capacity) result in META revisiting its framework for opex/capex just one quarter after providing it? We don’t believe so – in our view, the next update on opex and capex from META mgmt would be more likely in early 2026 after the completion of annual business planning process but that the current forecast also envisions a quite robust investment program; & 2) Does the launch of AI generative video and feed platforms (Sora 2, Veo 3, etc.) challenge the competitive positioning of Instagram? – Unlikely in our view and still far from a certain answer given the scale with an acknowledgement that widespread generation and dissemination of AI videos remains with more questions than answers on consumer appetite, IP protections and sustained long-term trends relative to existing short/long form video landscape. Turning back to operating trends, we continue to remain focused on forward revenue trends based on drivers sch as its content recommendation engine, closing the gap between engagement and monetization in short form video and the rising adoption rate and budget spend around Advantage+. Recent developments around the company’s AI efforts (future model releases, investments in AI talent and businesses, etc.) and how they are framed by management on the earnings call will likely remain a key area of investor focus (as it relates to the long-term implications for investment levels, potential revenue contribution and compounded earnings growth).
n Alphabet (GOOGL, Buy, \$288 PT) – We continue to highlight GOOGL as one of the most positively levered AI companies inside our border coverage universe and such a view has become more universally accepted among investors with the stock up +50% since the publication (link) of our last earnings preview (vs the S&P 500 +20%). The combination of growth in the usage of the Gemini app, continued growth in core search (our checks point to a reacceleration in Q3 vs Q2) and the search antitrust decision being more positive than feared in its remedies (link) have all resulted in a healthy re-rating of the shares. From this point, we see upward estimate revisions as the likely driver of sustained stock performance from current levels – our own industry work would point to sustained growth in Search, emerging monetization across AI canvasses, greater distribution of their AI solutions across the consumer and enterprise computing landscape, the growth in both revenue backlog and revenue conversion within Google Cloud & sustained growth across YouTube properties in both ad and subscription supported monetization (link). On expenses, we still see GOOGL providing an upward trajectory to GAAP operating income vs. forward Street estimates, yet recognize that upward pressure to AI investments may mute the scope of this outperformance.

Q3 Digital Ad Checks - Momentum Continues In Key Pockets of Spend; Focus Shifts to Q4 & 2026 Visibility
As detailed above, approaching the Q3 earnings season our industry channel checks and 3rd party data sources point to an overall environment that is better than feared but with continued low visibility into budget trends through year-end and into 2026. It remains a very “idiosyncratic” environment where we believe platform performance will be dictated by relative exposure to certain pockets of ad spend (by industry, ad objective, geography, size, etc.)
A few more specific themes/narratives emerged from our industry work, which we summarize below:
n Performance by Industry Vertical – Industries with heightened exposure to tariffs/uncertainty in the end demand environment performed overall better than feared in Q3 but still remain volatile & have lack of visibility into Q4 and 2026 forward demand trends - those include online travel, autos and consumer electronics. Within both eCommerce/retail and CPG, relative brand exposure to cross-border trade, discretionary vs. non-discretionary, etc. is creating a bifurcation in budget performances.
Brand vs. Direct Response – As mentioned above, brand advertising spend remains very volatile (being the first to be cut during periods of economic volatility) and subject to budget pullbacks as we look ahead. Direct response spend, while subject to some potential spend pullback (on an absolute basis), remains relatively more resilient and tied to consumer end-demand trends.
n User growth/engagement - User growth & engagement trends remain \~stable to rising in the US while seeing stronger growth in international markets and overall continuing to surprise to the upside (albeit seeing a slight deceleration towards the end of Q3). Short-form video continues to be a driver of incremental engagement. Based on data from SensorTower, we call out Instagram, Pinterest, YouTube and Facebook as seeing notably strong global user growth/engagement trends in Q3.
Pricing - Based on our channel checks, Q3 pricing trends across the digital advertising landscape were \~stable YoY (with slight growth in the US offset by decreases globally).

Pricing Trends - Stable Growth Trends In Q3
Based on our channel checks, Q3 pricing trends across the digital advertising landscape overall showed slight growth YoY as advertiser demand remained somewhat stable in the US (while experiencing some decreases globally). For Meta, specifically, data from Gupta Media shows that average US CPMs paid across Facebook & Instagram in Q3 were down \~(4)% QoQ and up \~3% YoY (lapping a \~9% YoY increase in Q3’24). Globally and by ad format, Instagram Feed CPMs decreased (16)% YoY ((11)% QoQ), Instagram Stories CPMs decreased (14)% YoY ((13)% QoQ) and Instagram Reels CPMs decreased (8)% YoY (+16% QoQ) in Q3.
Source: Gupta Media, Data compiled by Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research
Away from the month-to-month volatility, overall pricing for META properties is still well above pre-COVID levels, with US & global CPMs (by format) still tracking at \~1.5-2x and \~2-4x Q3’19 levels, respectively.

User Growth & Engagement Trends Remain Healthy, With Pockets of Strength in International & From Key Formats (incl. Short-Form Video) Data from SensorTower indicates that user growth & total time spent in app remains somewhat stable in the US while seeing stronger growth in international markets and overall continuing to surprise to the upside (albeit seeing a slight deceleration towards the end of Q3). We call out four platforms that are seeing particularly strong engagement trends in Q3: Instagram (total time spent up +17% YoY and +16% YoY globally & in the US, respectively), Pinterest (+14% YoY / +21% YoY), YouTube (+1% YoY /+5% YoY), and Facebook ((1)% YoY / +3% YoY).
The platforms that have seen the largest monthly average user growth since Jan 2021 levels are Reddit, Pinterest, and Instagram in the US and Reddit, Snapchat and Instagram globally, according to SensorTower. Short-Form Video Remains Key Driver of Engagement Growth for Instagram & YouTube
As we’ve discussed in prior research (link | link), short-form video remains a dominant theme within digital advertising and continues to be a key driver of engagement growth (time spent, sessions per day, etc.) for several of the major US platforms. To track this theme, we analyze data from SensorTower on user growth & engagement for what we consider to be the three primary short-form video platforms: TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. The data indicates that average time spent per user per day continues to increase for both Instagram (\~52 mins daily in the US and \~71 mins globally in Q3, vs. \~37 mins and \~54 mins in Q3’21, respectively) and YouTube (\~79 mins daily in the US and \~83 mins globally in Q3, vs. \~62 mins and \~71 mins in Q3’21, respectively). For TikTok, average US time spent per user per day was \~78 mins/day, down from \~85 mins/day in Q3’21 and a peak of \~92 mins/day in mid 2023.

Reels remains accretive to overall time spent for Instagram (as outlined above) and is a key driver of Reels exceeding revenue neutrality for Instagram (time spent increases outweighing headwinds from the monetization gap between Reels & Feed/Stories). On the monetization gap, according to Tinuiti, Reels still only represented \~21% of total Instagram ad impressions in Q2’25, and Instagram Reels CPMs, while increasing, were still at a \~38% discount to Instagram Feed CPMs on average in Q3’24. While we don’t expect Reels CPMs to ever reach full parity to Feed CPMs for a number of reasons (despite being a mature ad unit, Stories CPMs are still at a \~10-20% discount to Feed CPMs based on our ad checks; structural monetization gap for short-form video as a format, etc.), we still see a sizable opportunity for Reels to remain a key revenue growth tailwind for META in the coming years as the CPM gap closes further and as Reels continues to increase as a % of total ad impressions.

We downgrade our rating on IBTA from Neutral to Sell and lower our 12-month PT to \$26 (from \$30 prior). Consistent with our prior reports (link | link | link), we frame the Ibotta investment thesis across three key areas: (1) addressable market opportunity; (2) revenue growth outlook; & (3) margins & operating leverage. As outlined below, our visibility / conviction level into multiple of these areas has decreased and, against what we now see as a negatively skewed risk/reward, we downgrade our rating from Neutral to Sell.
Addressable Market And Long-Term 3P Supply Opportunity Remains Intact…
Ibotta remains exposed to two large addressable market opportunities: (1) the total US grocery market (GSe \~\$1.61trn in 2024E, growing at a \~3% ’24-‘28E CAGR); & (2) the total US advertising market (GSe \~\$588bn in 2024E, growing at a \~5% ’24-‘28E CAGR). For both addressable markets, we expect steady industry growth and secular tailwinds from increasing digital penetration (with online channels for both US grocery spend & US advertising spend to continue to outpace overall industry growth).
We also still see Ibotta as having a large opportunity to grow into its current 3P supply base over the long-term – through 3P partnerships with Walmart, Instacart & others. For Walmart specifically, we estimate Ibotta 3P redeemers currently represent \~12% of total Walmart US weekly shoppers, which we expect to grow to \~15% by the end of 2028. This informs our expectation for steady 3P redeemer growth for IBTA, from \~15.4mm at year-end 2024 to \~24.5mm by year-end 2028 (\~12% 4-year CAGR). Outside of Walmart, we forecast non-Walmart publishers to grow from \~1.6mm at year-end 2024 to \~3.0mm by year-end 2026 and \~4.8mm by year-end 2028 (or comprising \~35% of Ibotta’s total 4-year 3P redeemer growth) – we look to future periods to see how these newer partnerships are scaling (including Instacart & DoorDash in particular).

The PP&E market cycle is entering its middle stages of recovery. Using Progressive’s (PGR) and Allstate’s (ALL) combined total auto policy in force growth as a proxy for industry recovery, according to GS GIR estimates, growth is expected to begin moderating to \~MSD % growth into 2026 (lapping peak growth rates in Q1’25). GS Factor Profile The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
